title: Production Computer Vision API (Object Detection & OCR)
problem: Deploying deep learning computer vision models directly from research notebooks into production web services frequently results in high latency, memory starvation, and severe concurrency bottlenecks. Naive per-request inference under Python locks the interpreter and fails to utilize batching opportunities. This project builds an asynchronous model serving API in FastAPI that executes object detection and optical character recognition using ONNX Runtime, featuring dynamic request batching, pre-allocated tensor memory, image validation and resizing pipelines, and structured bounding box JSON output formatting.
use_cases: Automated document and invoice processing with bounding box OCR coordinate extraction
Digital identity verification and visual quality assessment for automated user onboarding
Real-time object detection and safety equipment verification for industrial site cameras
hard_parts: Coordinating dynamic request batching across asynchronous HTTP workers without introducing latency penalties on single requests
Optimizing image preprocessing (letterboxing, color normalization) to avoid becoming the primary throughput bottleneck
Managing ONNX Runtime session execution providers and CPU thread pool allocations to prevent host thrashing
Parsing and filtering multi-class bounding box coordinates with Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) within sub-millisecond budgets
screener_signals: FastAPI service with ONNX Runtime model inference decoupled from HTTP worker threads
Automated benchmarking harness establishing CPU inference latency and batch throughput
Anti-fake verification script evaluating dynamically transformed image inputs and asserting bounding box accuracy

components.name: Image Preprocessing Pipeline
components.purpose: Decodes raw image bytes, validates dimensions, normalizes pixels, and applies letterbox resizing

components.name: Dynamic Batching Ingress Queue
components.purpose: Aggregates concurrent incoming inference requests into batches of up to 8 images within 15ms windows

components.name: ONNX Runtime Inference Engine
components.purpose: Executes quantized object detection model on CPU using multi-threaded execution providers

components.name: NMS Post-Processing Filter
components.purpose: Applies Non-Maximum Suppression and confidence thresholding to generate clean bounding boxes

components.name: Async Prediction Gateway
components.purpose: Exposes multipart/form-data upload endpoints and streams JSON detection coordinates

components.name: Containerized Service Package
components.purpose: Encapsulates model weights and runtime dependencies for consistent cross-platform execution

architecture.data_flow: Clients upload image files via HTTP POST to FastAPI; the Preprocessing Pipeline decodes and resizes images to 640x640 tensors; requests enter the Dynamic Batching Ingress Queue; when the batch fills or timeout expires, ONNX Runtime executes inference; the Post-Processing Filter applies Non-Maximum Suppression; individual prediction results resolve to client response futures and return formatted bounding boxes.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Image dimension and format validation rejecting corrupted files; timeout enforcement on inference queue preventing client connection hangs.

targets.method: Benchmark measuring model execution duration for a single 640x640 image on CPU
targets.input: Single synthetic 640x640 JPEG image passed to ONNX Runtime session
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, ONNX Runtime 1.16+, warm model session
targets.minimum_pass: Inference latency < 120ms per image on CPU
targets.target: Inference latency < 75ms per image on CPU
targets.report: Benchmark execution timing log with 50-run mean and p95 percentiles

targets.method: Autocannon load benchmark sending 20 concurrent image prediction requests
targets.input: Continuous stream of 200 synthetic JPEG images sent across 10 concurrent HTTP clients
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Docker container, local loopback
targets.report: Autocannon summary report reporting requests per second and latency distribution

targets.metric: Mean Average Precision (mAP@50) on Evaluation Set
targets.method: Evaluation of object detection bounding boxes against ground-truth annotations
targets.input: Labelled held-out test split of 200 synthetic evaluation images with 600 annotated objects
targets.minimum_pass: mAP@50 score >= 0.60 on evaluation test split
targets.target: mAP@50 score >= 0.72 on evaluation test split
targets.report: Evaluation script summary report reporting mAP@50, precision, and recall metrics

starter_input.spec: Pre-trained quantized YOLOv8n ONNX model weights and labelled synthetic test image dataset.
starter_input.size: 1 quantized ONNX model file (approx 12MB) and 200 synthetic test images with JSON bounding box labels
starter_input.seeded_cases: Varying image aspect ratios (square, portrait, landscape), low-contrast images, overlapping objects, and corrupted image bytes
starter_input.label_source: Public synthetic evaluation dataset annotated with deterministic COCO-format bounding boxes
starter_input.personal_data_policy: Strictly synthetic and public domain object images; zero real personal faces or private documents used

prerequisites: Intermediate Python programming (asyncio, type hints, pytest)
Fundamental computer vision concepts (tensors, bounding boxes, IoU, mAP, NMS)
Familiarity with REST APIs and multipart file upload handling

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU-bound ONNX Runtime inference)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid GPUs, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Python 3.11 and Docker installed
environment.fallback_path: Local Python virtual environment without Docker using PyTorch CPU model weights

riskiest_component.name: Inference Latency Spike Under Heavy Concurrency on CPU
riskiest_component.fallback: Set strict concurrency limits in uvicorn and bound dynamic batch size to 4 images max on 4-core machines

Screener verification script executing predictions and dynamic validation in under 2 minutes
out_of_scope: Fine-tuning foundational vision models from scratch
Video stream frame extraction and RTSP streaming
resources: ONNX Runtime Python API reference documentation
FastAPI multipart form data and streaming response tutorial
Ultralytics YOLOv8 export and inference guides

rubric.expected_result: API responds with HTTP 200 and JSON payload containing detected classes and coordinates
rubric.evidence_location: Terminal HTTP response headers and JSON body
rubric.pass_criterion: HTTP status 200 with valid bounding box coordinates and confidence score > 0.5

rubric.input: Benchmark evaluation test script python scripts/evaluate_model.py
rubric.action: Run evaluation across 200 labelled test images
rubric.expected_result: Script computes mAP@50 score against ground truth annotations
rubric.pass_criterion: Reported mAP@50 score is >= 0.60 across the 200 evaluation images

rubric.input: Autocannon load test simulating 10 concurrent users uploading images
rubric.expected_result: API maintains batching queue and responds without dropping requests
rubric.pass_criterion: Average throughput exceeds 15 images/sec with 0 socket errors

rubric.input: Corrupted non-image file uploaded to /predict endpoint
rubric.action: Send text file as image upload to test validation
rubric.expected_result: API rejects invalid payload with structured HTTP 422 error response
rubric.pass_criterion: HTTP status 422 returned with clear validation error message

rubric.expected_result: Script posts image, asserts returned bounding box overlaps target coordinates with IoU > 0.7
rubric.pass_criterion: Returned bounding box matches injected rectangle coordinates with exit code 0

worksheet.q1: The student builds an asynchronous computer vision model serving API in FastAPI that executes object detection on CPU using ONNX Runtime, dynamic request batching, and NMS post-processing.
worksheet.q2: Core path: ONNX model conversion, FastAPI inference endpoints, dynamic batching queue, and mAP evaluation (29h). Extended path: GPU TensorRT acceleration and OCR pipeline (+14h).
worksheet.q3: Components: Model Setup (5h), Dynamic Queue (5h), FastAPI API (4h), Evaluation Benchmark (4h), Load Testing (4h), Docs & Buffer (3h). Total 25h x 1.15 = 29h.
worksheet.q4: Project types: ML serving/vision/NLP/LLM/RAG, API/backend. Metrics: Single-Image Inference Latency, Batch Processing Throughput, mAP@50. Rejected: training loss convergence (serving project).
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: dynamic batching without queue starvation, letterbox preprocessing performance, ONNX thread allocation, and NMS post-processing.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: pre-trained quantized YOLOv8n ONNX model (12MB) and 200 synthetic test images with COCO labels. No personal data.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: local venv without Docker.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: CPU inference latency under load. Fallback: bound batch size to 4 items max.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: static JSON responses. Anti-fake check 5 generates a dynamic synthetic image with colored rectangles at random coordinates and asserts returned IoU > 0.7.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; synthetic and public domain object images only; no face identification.
